new_entities.name: Soy-based infant formula
new_entities.description: Modern soy protein isolate-based infant formula used as an alternative to cow's-milk formula.

new_entities.name: General infant outcomes
aliases: growth and developmental outcomes in infancy
new_entities.description: Broad infant outcomes including growth, tolerance, hydration, and neurodevelopment-related safety endpoints.

edges.effect_quant: The most consistent finding is neutrality: modern soy formulas generally support normal growth and short-term clinical outcomes comparable with other standard feeding options in infants who need them.
edges.population: term infants fed modern soy protein isolate-based infant formula
edges.mechanism: Modern soy formulas are nutritionally engineered to support growth despite lower intrinsic methionine and the presence of phytates and phytoestrogens. The key biologic concern has been endocrine or developmental disruption, but the better human safety literature has not shown a strong clinically important signal.
edges.summary: The literature is more reassuring than enthusiastic. Modern soy formula appears to support normal growth, gastrointestinal tolerance, and broad short-term safety outcomes, but it does not show clear superiority over cow's-milk formula or human milk for routine infant development, so the right framing is acceptable neutrality rather than benefit.
edges.caveats: Much of the soy-formula safety literature is observational, industry-linked, or not designed to detect subtle long-term endocrine outcomes. This edge should be read as 'generally acceptable when indicated,' not as a recommendation to prefer soy formula for most healthy infants.
